cases.name: Gayatri Balasamy v. ISG Novasoft Technologies Ltd.
cases.court: Supreme Court of India, Constitution Bench
cases.facts: The Constitution Bench considered the scope of judicial power under Section 34 in challenges to arbitral awards.
cases.issue: Whether and to what extent a court hearing a Section 34 application can modify an arbitral award.
cases.ratioDecidendi: The Court recognised a limited power in specified circumstances but rejected any general merits-based appellate power over arbitral awards.
cases.holding: Section 34 remains a narrow supervisory remedy; any intervention must stay within the statutory and judicially recognised limits.
cases.relevance: Current Constitution Bench authority for the scope of Section 34 review and modification.

cases.name: Associate Builders v. Delhi Development Authority
cases.facts: The Court examined the grounds on which an arbitral award could be set aside under Section 34.
cases.issue: What constitutes conflict with public policy and what is the permissible scope of judicial interference?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Public-policy review is structured by the statutory grounds and cannot become a merits appeal.
cases.holding: The Court articulated the principal public-policy categories then applicable under Section 34.
cases.relevance: Foundational authority on public policy review under Section 34, read subject to subsequent statutory and Supreme Court developments.

cases.name: Ssangyong Engineering & Construction Co. Ltd. v. National Highways Authority of India
cases.facts: The Court considered a Section 34 challenge after the 2015 amendments.
cases.issue: What is the permissible scope of judicial intervention after the amended Section 34 regime?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The amended Section 34 limits judicial intervention and the court cannot effectively reassess the merits of the award.
cases.holding: The Court applied the post-amendment narrow review framework.
cases.relevance: Key post-2015 authority on Section 34, subject to later Supreme Court clarification.
